reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes earning money through Binance and PancakeSwap, provides destination links including a Binance referral-style link, and instructs viewers to put crypto into liquidity, stake LP tokens for CAKE rewards, and use Binance locked staking. It repeatedly presents returns such as 38.15% and 29%, alongside compounding-profit language and wallet-connection interfaces, framing the content as a crypto wealth solicitation rather than a neutral market discussion. The speaker states that this is not investment advice and that money is at risk, and the available video evidence does not claim verified returns, completed transactions, or actual losses.

Cake BNB so far it was paying us 38.15%
In Binance we can put a staking blocked of 30, 90, 120 days
that will pay us a 29% of the 19th annual investment

opening.argument: The presentation is materially qualified rather than deceptive. The speaker expressly tells viewers that “this is not an investment advice,” acknowledges that “your money is in play,” and makes the decision the viewer’s own. He also directs viewers to “study the 2 exchanges and study the 2 proposals” before deciding. Those warnings communicate uncertainty and risk, making the content better understood as conditional commentary about possible returns than as a guarantee or concealed solicitation.

citations.quote: this is not an investment advice since
your money is in play, the one they are going to put at risk, your choice is what you decide to make
study the 2 exchanges and study the 2 proposals

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited rates and staking references describe what the speaker is analyzing, but they do not establish a guaranteed outcome. The reference argument itself concedes that there is no verified return, completed transaction, or loss. That concession is consistent with the speaker’s explicit risk warning and instruction to study the proposals, rather than with a disguised promise.

citations.quote: study everything I just said
your choice is what you decide to make

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A disclaimer does not undo the substance of the pitch. The title expressly presents combining the platforms “to increase profits,” while the speaker gives concrete return figures and says profits can produce more profits. Telling viewers to decide for themselves does not show that the advertised mechanism or returns are reliable; it merely shifts the risk to them.

citations.quote: How to earn money by combining binance and pancakeswap to increase profits
our profits come to work they give us more profits and those profits give us more profit
Cake BNB so far it was paying us 38.15%

opening.argument: The material is structured as an operational walkthrough. The speaker explains how liquidity produces an LP token, how that token is placed into staking, how to compare options, and how to calculate examples. The supplied frames show a PancakeSwap farming table, a price chart with a calculator, and a Binance Earn table with different durations. That combination supports a tutorial or demonstration of exchange tools and yield calculations, not proof that viewers were asked to transfer funds to the creator.

citations.quote: the first thing we have to do as always is invest in liquidity
In Binance we can put a staking blocked of 30, 90, 120 days

rebuttal.rebuttal: Showing platform interfaces and explaining calculations does not by itself convert an educational demonstration into a scam. The reference opening identifies no creator-controlled wallet, completed deposit, or credential request. The pages shown are recognizable exchange and farming interfaces, and the spoken content explains how the displayed figures are interpreted.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The tutorial format is precisely how the solicitation is delivered. The speaker does not merely explain interface mechanics: he says viewers must invest in liquidity, presents the process as producing profit, and recommends leaving assets locked. Screenshots of legitimate-looking interfaces do not validate the promoter’s claims or establish that the advertised returns will materialize.

opening.argument: The content points viewers toward ordinary, identifiable platform services rather than an unexplained private investment pool. The description provides the PancakeSwap site, a Binance site, and a separate account-creation video; the presentation discusses platform-listed products and their stated terms. The Binance screen visibly presents selectable durations and subscription controls, while the PancakeSwap screen displays liquidity-pool options. Nothing supplied shows the creator requesting viewers’ passwords, credentials, or direct deposits to a personal account, and no downline-income mechanism appears.

citations.quote: PANCAKESWAP LINK: https://pancakeswap.finance/
Binance link: https://www.binance.me/es-la/activity/referral-entry/cpa?fromactivitypage=true&ref=cpa_00tbve9bfx

rebuttal.rebuttal: A referral-style URL and platform links can indicate ordinary promotion of external services; they do not prove that the creator controls those services or receives viewers’ funds. The reference argument also relies on the existence of platform screens, but a displayed product and a stated rate are not evidence of a scam mechanism. The supplied material shows no personal-wallet collection or credential harvesting.

citations.quote: Binance link: https://www.binance.me/es-la/activity/referral-entry/cpa?fromactivitypage=true&ref=cpa_00tbve9bfx

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a personal wallet does not resolve the concern: the alleged mechanism is participation in liquidity provision and staking, not necessarily payment to the speaker. The description funnels viewers to account creation and platform links, while the video instructs them to invest and lock assets based on projected returns. Calling the services ordinary does not substantiate the promised profitability.
